mxCell.value: DocuFlow — where a model is called, and what it is allowed to decide

Six model calls. Four of them cannot change a value: two only read, one only ranks facts computed before it was asked, one compiles a rule once and is never consulted again. Everything between the reading and the ledger — merging, grounding, validation, routing, posting — is deterministic code.
model call
deterministic code
tool the agent may call
guard / refusal
Solid arrow = data flow. Dashed = a constraint on the call.
1 · READ THE PAGE
Rendered page images PDF → 1800px, max 8 pages (PDFium, behind a process lock)

OCR — vision model prompt: ocr/prompts.py v15_prompt(figure_language) "Return the page as Markdown. Tables as HTML. Transcribe, do not summarise or interpret." output: page text + table markup, per page

Engine, picked at runtime ollama · Typhoon OCR 1.5 3B — native /api/generate, keep_alive 30m, num_ctx 8192 (the OpenAI-compatible endpoint silently ignores both) typhoon_api · Typhoon Cloud OCR v1.5 openai · gpt-5.1 vision · claude · sonnet-5 vision pdftext · text layer only, no model tesseract · offline last resort
Quality score (deterministic) character mix, line shape, gibberish ratio → feeds every field's confidence → marks the run degraded
2 · WHAT KIND OF DOCUMENT IS THIS
Keyword pre-classifier (deterministic, first) distinctive words per schema — "ใบกำกับภาษี", "PURCHASE ORDER" confident → the model is never called
Classifier — LLM, only when unsure system: CLASSIFIER_SYSTEM · "Output JSON only." user: classification_prompt(first ~2k chars) → {doc_type, confidence, reason}
DocumentSchema from the registry invoice · receipt · purchase_order · contract · form · unknown fields, aliases, choices, required / critical flags, the record kind it posts into
3 · READ THE FIELDS — TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY

Channel 1 — field-first agents/llm_extractor.py system: EXTRACTION_SYSTEM "Copy values exactly as printed. Never calculate, never convert, never infer. Not found → null. Every value needs the verbatim line it came from." user: extraction_prompt(schema, document_text) one line per field: name (type) — description, aliases → {field: {raw_value, evidence}}

Channel 2 — label-first agents/verify_extractor.py system: VERIFY_SYSTEM "Find the label on the page, then take what sits beside it. Work from the page, not from what an invoice usually says." user: verification_prompt(schema, document_text) → the same shape, reached a different way

Constraints on channel 2 llm/factory.resolve_verify_llm • a different backend from channel 1 — two runs of one model repeat the same mistake, and the agreement signal is then worth nothing • never the backend hosting OCR: it evicts the vision model and a document went from 40s to over 10 minutes • LLM_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 90 • on timeout or no second model → fall back to the deterministic label matcher, so a keyless run still gets a cross-check rather than dropping to one channel
Neither channel sees the other's answer. That is the entire point: agreement between two blind readings is evidence, agreement after seeing the first answer is an echo.
4 · MERGE AND GROUND — NO MODEL PAST THIS LINE

Normalise normalize/* dates → YYYY-MM-DD (Buddhist era, Thai digits, day-first detected from components > 12, re-read from the evidence quote) money → float · tax IDs → checksum enums → schema choice_aliases ("PAID BY VISA ****4412" → credit_card)

Ground the evidence agents/grounding.py 1. is the quote really on the page? fuzzy match ≥ 88 (OCR noise is not a lie) 2. does the quote actually state the value? type-aware: dates compared as dates, amounts as numbers, enums exempt (a schema word never appears on a page)

Score the field confidence.py both channels agree → 0.97 one channel, grounded → 0.86 channels disagree → 0.45 one channel, ungrounded → 0.30 × OCR quality, × critical-field penalty Corroboration: two channels agreeing and both quotes real on the page ⇒ grounded, even if neither quote passes the strict value test.

Derive currency normalize/locale.py symbol or code on the page → grounded ("$154.06" states its currency) else vendor's registered currency else the country the document is from (earliest marker wins — the issuer is at the top, the ship-to below) → inferred, never grounded, cannot auto-post
An ungrounded critical field can never post on its own, whatever the model claimed.
5 · VALIDATE — DETERMINISTIC, NEVER MODEL-JUDGED
26 built-in rules rules/*.py arithmetic · dates · master data · duplicates three-way match · tax IDs · bank accounts each declares doc types, severity and aliases
Rules the user wrote rules/custom.py stored as a condition tree, evaluated by rules/expressions.py — no eval, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 12 branches. A model compiled it once; a model never runs it.

Execution policy policy.py (persisted) rules_free_mode → nothing runs at all builtin_rules_disabled → ours off, yours on disabled_rules → individual ids rule_severity → re-grade without silencing Each mode emits its own marker finding, so a record that was not checked never looks like one that was.
Isolation a rule that raises becomes a warning finding — one broken rule cannot stop validation
6 · EXPLAIN THE FAILURE — TOOL-CALLING AGENT (only when a check already failed)
See page 3 — the reconciler's tool loop, its seven tools, and the vetting step that refuses a correction the page does not support.
Pipeline — bytes in, a validated ledger entry out
Every stage appends to the run's trace, and every stage is defensive: a failure degrades the run and routes it to a person rather than raising.
Ingest upload · URL fetch (private ranges blocked) · sample content-addressed blob, SHA-256
render PDFium → images module-level lock: two workers rendering at once segfaulted the interpreter

preprocess straighten · relight · sharpen each correction gated on a measurement, applied, measured again, and reverted if the number did not improve a clean PDF passes through untouched and writes no file the prepared page is written beside the original, never over it
ocr vision model (model)
classify keywords, then model if unsure (model)
extract channel 1 + channel 2 (2 models) then merge, ground, score — no model
line_items table rows from HTML markup or text a line that parses as a date is not a line item
validate master data + rules vendor match: tax ID → exact name → alias → core name → fuzzy ≥ 86
route routing.decide() auto_post needs ALL of: no blocking failure, confidence ≥ threshold, every required field present, every critical field grounded
reconcile tool-calling agent (model) runs only if something failed — nothing on the happy path
archive hard link into data/archive///
post the only write into the ledger refuses anything not cleared for auto_post unless a reviewer forced it
Review queue a person sees the page beside every field, its evidence quote, every rule that ran and the agent's account
Save keeps the corrected values, re-runs the rules, and leaves the routing decision exactly where it was. A save is an edit, not a verdict.

Re-check revalidate.py replays master data → rules → confidence → routing against the stored run. No render, no OCR, no model: the values did not change, the policy did. Seven documents re-judged in 25 ms.
Approve & post refused while a blocking rule still fails. The reviewer corrects the values or rejects the document — there is no way to approve past a failing check.

Two refusals that shape re-checking • a document a person rejected is never posted by a re-evaluation — a policy change is not consent to overturn someone's decision • a posted document is refused outright: a posted record is corrected downstream, not by re-running a check

Which value is wrong rules/repair.py The amounts are tied together by three relations: the lines sum to the subtotal, the tax is a rate applied to it, the subtotal and tax make the total. One misread value breaks every relation it appears in and leaves the others standing, so what still holds names what broke. Exactly one field explains it → name it, carry the value. Two would → say nothing. A wrong number wearing a suggestion's confidence is worse than no suggestion. Then name the slip: a transposition, a decimal point, a digit pair scans confuse. A reviewer confirms that with a glance instead of re-deriving it.

Two tolerances, not one An invoice may differ from the purchase order it quotes by 2% — freight, a part shipment, a price that moved. It may not differ from itself by more than rounding. Lending the commercial allowance to a document's own arithmetic let an 810-baht misread post as "totals add up".
Batch queue jobs.py ThreadPoolExecutor, worker count by engine: local engine → 1 worker (one model, one GPU) cloud engine → 4 workers max 50 files per batch
The three agents that use tools or write prose — and what each is prevented from doing
RECONCILER — agents/reconciler.py
Runs only when a check has already failed. Nothing on the happy path.

system: RECONCILER_SYSTEM "You are an accounts-payable analyst reviewing an automated extraction before it posts to the ledger. Verify with tools before you conclude. Never assert a value you have not confirmed with a tool. Propose a correction only when read_document shows that exact value on the page; if the correct value is not printed, say so and recommend review instead. Finish with JSON only."

user: reconciliation_prompt(...) doc_type every populated field, its value and confidence, marked [UNVERIFIED] where ungrounded the fields that came back empty every failed check, with severity and message + the exact JSON shape to answer in loop: MAX_ITERATIONS 6 · max_tokens 3000 temperature 0 · history trimmed to 40 messages tool results truncated to 2,500 chars
THE SEVEN TOOLS — agents/tools.py
read_document what the page actually says — the only source a correction may come from
lookup_vendor the vendor master file
lookup_purchase_order the PO register
lookup_contract the contract register
find_posted_records confirm a suspected duplicate
check_arithmetic any sum — the model never adds up itself
validate_tax_id Thai check digit
Every tool is read-only. None of them can write a field, a record or a master row.

VETTING — the corrections are re-grounded before a human sees them for each proposed correction: field must exist in the schema · the quoted evidence must be findable on the page (fuzzy ≥ 88) · the quote must actually state the proposed value A correction that fails any of these is shown as ungrounded and cannot be applied. Measured on a real document: the agent proposed replacing the subtotal — the one change that would have made the arithmetic check pass — and the guard refused it, because two channels had already read and agreed that number.
RULE AUTHORING — rules/authoring.py
The model runs once, at authoring time. It never runs the rule.
1. a person types plain language "Invoices over 100,000 baht must quote a purchase order"

2. AUTHORING_SYSTEM compiles it to one JSON rule {rule_id, message, doc_types, severity, when, assert} explicit polarity: `assert` is what must be TRUE MAX_ATTEMPTS 2 — a rejected draft is retried with the validator's own error message fed back in

3. validated as an expression tree rules/expressions.py no eval, no code execution · depth ≤ 8 · ≤ 12 branches only known fields and operators a test that can never fail is refused ("vendor_matched present" is true even when it is False)
4. previewed against documents already processed the author sees which of their real documents it would have failed, before saving it

5. saved — and from here it is plain code evaluated by the expression engine on every document, for ever. It always answers to exactly what the author approved, and it keeps running when the built-in rules are switched off.
BRIEFING — agents/briefing.py
The model writes the covering note. It never supplies the facts.

1. the agenda is computed first store/attention.py payments due · contracts expiring · purchase orders committed and never billed · counterparties whose documents keep being held, and the rules holding them Every date, amount and count is SQL, not a model.

2. BRIEFING_SYSTEM ranks it no tools "You are given items that are already true. Never state a number, name or date that is not in the items given to you. Cite item ids in square brackets. Lead with what is late, then what is stuck." max_tokens 1200

3. every citation is checked back against the agenda an id that is not on it is dropped and the drop reported. Brackets are stripped before matching — the prompt shows ids as [CTR-2025-018] and rejecting that form would be the check enforcing punctuation rather than truth. What this cannot catch: real ids in a wrong relationship. Observed once — two purchase orders grouped under one supplier when they belong to two. The highlights carry computed headlines beside every claim, so the page contradicts the prose where it matters. Without a model the page still works, in duller words.
One rule holds across all three: a model may read, look up, propose and explain. It may never be the thing that decides a value is correct.
